title: consent-aware-observability-routing-epochal-scrub-playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As Redwood scales, observability streams (traces, metrics, logs) increasingly contain token-like or PII-bearing values emitted by customer workloads and SDKs. Existing scrubbers are reactive and inconsistent across ingestion paths (agent -> ingest -> pipeline -> datastore). This ticket defines a coordinated playbook for consent-aware routing, epochal retention windows, and a low-latency scrub-before-index proxy to limit exposure and make retention auditable.

Problem statement: We need a standardized, low-latency mechanism that ensures: (1) tenant/trace-level consent flags affect routing and retention decisions early, (2) PII is removed or pseudonymized before long-term indexing where required, and (3) RBAC and access logs capture any just-in-time reveals. Current gaps: inconsistent pipeline scrub order, no epochal retention concept, and limited linkage between consent and routing.

Goals: 
- Enforce consent-scoped routing so events marked with ‘no_pii_index’ are routed to ephemeral stores only.
- Introduce epochal retention windows per tenant (hot -> warm -> cold) with automated erasure for PII-bearing fields at defined epochs.
- Provide a scrub-proxy that can operate in-path (low-latency) for critical fields and a downstream scrub service for heavier transformations.
- Emit immutable access logs and RBAC checks for any manual/unmask operations.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace existing legal-deletion hooks for subpoena requests or build a full consent-management UI (that is PM scope). It also does not change token billing semantics.

High-level approach: 
1) Consent tag propagation: augment trace/ingest proto with a small consent header set (consent_level, epoch_hint, tenant_policy_hash). SDKs and edge agents will propagate these.
2) Routing rules engine: implement a lightweight routing layer (Observability Router) that reads consent headers and tenant policy to decide: local-ephemeral-store, scrub-proxy, or full-index. Rules are programmable and evaluated before batching.
3) Scrub-proxy (in-path): a fast, typed-scrubber that performs field-level safe-redaction (hashing, truncation, token masking) for a configurable policy set. Implemented in Rust and compiled to a small binary to run at ingress for minimal added latency.
4) Epochal retention controller: a metadata service that tracks per-tenant epoch boundaries and triggers downstream scrubbing/compaction jobs that remove or pseudonymize PII fields when data transitions from hot->warm/cold.
5) Access & audit ledger: every time data is promoted for long-term indexing or an unmask is requested, append a signed entry to an immutable ledger (with actor, reason, TTL). Integrate with RBAC checks from the identity service.

Trade-offs and risks: 
- Performance vs completeness: in-path scrub must be minimal to keep tail latency; heavier NLP-based PII detection will live downstream, which risks short-term exposure in ephemeral stores. Mitigation: ephemeral stores have short TTL and encrypted-at-rest.
- Developer burden: requiring SDKs to set consent headers may take time; fallback to agent-side inference is necessary with logging for mismatches.
- Complexity: introducing routing layer increases op-surface. Keep rules simple and versioned.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Consent header schema committed and published in SDK docs.
- Observability Router prototype routes synthetic traces correctly to ephemeral vs index paths in test harness.
- In-path scrub-proxy runs with median added latency < 2ms at 95th percentile under benchmark load.
- Epochal retention controller triggers scrubbing jobs and downstream datasets show removed PII fields after epoch transition in staging.
- Audit ledger contains entries for all promotions/unmasks and is queryable by compliance team.

Migration and rollout: 
- Phase 1 (staging): deploy router + scrub-proxy in staging ingest path, enable for opt-in tenants. Run canary traffic and validate acceptance criteria.
- Phase 2 (limited-prod): enable for low-volume tenants with high privacy demands; monitor latency and errors for 2 weeks.
- Phase 3 (GA): flip default routing to require explicit opt-out to full-index for newly onboarded tenants; provide migration scripts for older data where tenant policies demand retroactive scrubbing.

Observability & dashboards: add a new console dashboard: 'Privacy Routing' showing routed volumes per tenant, scrub-proxy latency histogram, epoch transitions, and audit-log event rates. Hook existing error and latency alerts to P1 SLOs.

APIs and artifacts: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/obs-privacy-routing (internal).
Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/9123.
Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs-privacy-routing-staging.

Open questions: 
- Do we require policy hashing to be reversible for debug workflows, or only store policy IDs? (security team preference: store non-reversible hash)
- How aggressive should epoch TTLs be for ephemeral stores by default? Proposal: hot=7d, warm=30d, cold=180d.

Next steps: 
- Finish consent header proto + SDK docs (owner: SDK team, blocker).
- MVP scrub-proxy PoC and perf run (owner: infra/observability).
- Security review session scheduled (see activity).
